newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt six-month surplus NZ$323 mln above f/cast.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt six-month surplus NZ$323 mln above f/cast.

text.p: The New Zealand government's financial results for the first half of the 1996/97 year came in slightly ahead of expectation, Treasurer Winston Peters and Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Thursday.
The government's financial statements for the six months to December 31, 1996, show a net surplus of NZ$1.938 billion, $323 million more than forecast.
In a joint statement, Peters and Birch said the surplus reflected tax revenue and state-owned enterprise and government entity surpluses which were both higher than forecast.
The government's net worth improved to $5.484 billion, up $319 million on forecast.
Net public debt as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was 29.1 percent at December 31 compared with 29.3 percent at November 30.
"Debt servicing costs...have fallen for the six months from $2.1 billion in 1991/92 to $1.6 billion in 1996/97," Peters and Birch said.
